Well as governments fall into more and more debt, people are adverse to buying bonds because there's a fear that they won't be paid back in however many years' time.
So to offset the risk of putting all their money on the line and possibly losing it all, investors demand higher returns on the bonds that they buy.

62895525

What he said, the rate is set automatically through bond auctions. The difference between what the bond is worth and what institutions are willing to bid on buying that bond is the yield %, the yield sets the minimum rate for the rest of the market because why would you accept any less when you can just buy government bonds.

What happens when the yield gets too high is that the government starts considering straight money printing, that is putting money out into the economy without getting people to lock up their money for 10,20,30 years through buying bonds.
